direction: January brings provisional belonging, household humour and memory into a room being prepared, an attentive bird and a red sari in late light. Graphite, transparent watercolor and pastel vary the visual voice. Personal distress, exploitation and a call for simple poetry stay text-led.

items.title: A room not yet lived in
items.rationale: The new room offers possibility but cannot quiet the speaker’s unsettled inner life. A low view of preparation materials keeps that provisional feeling without inventing the person or making construction mess picturesque.

review.notes: PASS: room corner, slack crossed cords, cropped bucket and flat lid agree in perspective and contact. Paint residue is limited to the work object; broad clean floor conveys provisional occupancy without picturesque rubble. Quiet graphite/gouache and low viewpoint serve unease without an invented figure; independent:false.

items.alt: An unfinished room with a paint bucket and loose red and blue cords beside an empty grey floor.

items.title: The household commentator
items.rationale: The playful poem describes a talkative pet bird with strong preferences and a place in family life. A small green parakeet is an illustrative interpretation, not a claim about the poet’s actual pet or its species; attention and posture carry the humour without human costume.

review.notes: PASS: attentive head tilt, closed hooked beak, folded wings and long tail convey ordinary bird behaviour; both feet contact the perch, rear toes partly occluded. Soft uneven feather washes and quiet wall prevent cartoon performance. This generic parakeet is an interpretation of the talkative bird, not a claimed likeness or species identification of the actual pet; independent:false.

items.alt: A small green parakeet tilts its head on a wooden perch beside a cropped seed bowl and softly lit window.

items.title: Red cloth in the late light
items.rationale: The opening folds peace into a red sari before moving through memory and mortality. One loosely folded red cotton sari can hold embodied memory without inventing a dying woman, family photographs or religious montage.

review.notes: PASS: normal-size inspection finds weighted cloth folds resting coherently on the bed and falling toward the floor, consistent warm window light, quiet negative space and restrained pastel/gouache marks. The red sari carries the poem’s memory without inventing a woman or documentary portrait. Same-assistant review; independent:false.

items.alt: A red sari rests in loose folds across a plain wooden bed in warm late light.

text_led.rationale: The first-person night-time distress stays text-led without visualizing self-harm or inventing a suffering figure.
The Odia address about vulnerability and exploitation remains in its words; avoid literal predators, bodies or a moralizing portrait.
The invitation to let poems be simple and the translator credit deserve a generous text-led opening rather than a catalogue of its natural images.
